CDC progressed normally without a separate capture job, but stops progressing when the replication Log Reader Agent is stopped. Capture and replication must both be preserved. Which recovery addresses their documented shared dependency?

answerChoices.text: Resolve the Log Reader Agent stoppage and resume it so its shared log-reading path can feed both consumers.
Treat the absent dedicated CDC capture job as proof that CDC was never enabled.
Disable and recreate CDC solely to force a second independent capture path while retaining the publication.
Run CHECKPOINT and assume unprocessed captured changes no longer require log reading.

candidates.explanation: Restore the replication Log Reader Agent, which also serves CDC in this coexistence configuration.
candidates.deepExplanation: The absence of a separate capture job is not itself a fault when transactional replication supplies the shared reader. This diagnostic differs from ordinary CDC latency, retention gaps and captured-column schema transitions in the archived bank.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: A dedicated capture job is typical when CDC runs without transactional publications. The source explicitly describes its absence when the replication log reader performs capture instead.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: Reinitialization can be appropriate for an intentionally replaced capture configuration, but it is not the documented coexistence repair. The replication log reader is intentionally shared, and recreating capture can disrupt the retained consumer contract.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: Checkpoint can participate in normal log management, but the article says CDC-marked changes must be captured before their log truncation boundary advances. It cannot replace the stopped shared capture process.

candidates.question: A team plans a change event streaming (CES) proof of concept on Azure SQL Managed Instance, currently configured with the SQL Server 2022 update policy. It is evaluating the official CES overview retrieved September 16, 2026 and accepts a Preview feature only in a nonproduction pilot. Which platform recommendation and maturity label match that evidence?

answerChoices.text: Retain the 2022 update policy and mark CES generally available because the calendar has advanced.
Apply the SQL Server 2025 CU3 Azure Arc identity instructions as the only Managed Instance prerequisite.
Label CES GA on Managed Instance but Preview on every other SQL platform.
Plan an approved move to the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy and retain the Preview label.

candidates.explanation: Managed Instance CES requires the stated newer update policy and remains Preview in this evidence.
candidates.deepExplanation: Availability, platform prerequisites and maturity are independent facts. This item does not provide protocol-specific setup commands: the same overview notes AMQP deprecation and defers platform-specific migration details to other articles.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: The retrieved overview explicitly calls CES Preview and requires a newer Managed Instance update policy. A later calendar date does not independently change either documented requirement.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: The CU3/Arc or Azure VM note belongs to SQL Server 2025 Entra authentication support. It is relevant to that platform, not a substitute for the separate Managed Instance update-policy requirement.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: The overview lists Managed Instance among the Preview products. Product-specific support details do not supply an exception that makes Managed Instance CES generally available.
